_README: Platforms that cannot have some settings at all. A profile matches when every top-level statement of a configuration starts with its 'root' (or one of its 'roots') (structured documents are flattened to 'Root Key ... value' lines before analysis). A matched profile turns an undecided result (UNKNOWN / NOT_CONFIGURED) of the listed controls into N/A with the reason; it never overrides a PASS or FAIL backed by a line. Adding a platform (Azure NSG, GCP firewall rules) is a new entry here, not code.

profiles.name: AWS security group
profiles.reason: An AWS security group only filters traffic to and from its resources: it has no management plane, accounts, logging or time settings of its own, so this check does not apply

profiles.name: Terraform (HCL)
profiles.reason: A Terraform file declares cloud resources (security groups, network security rules, firewall rules): it has no device management plane, accounts, logging or time settings of its own, so this check does not apply

profiles.name: Azure network security group
profiles.reason: An Azure network security group only filters traffic to and from its subnets and interfaces: it has no management plane, accounts, logging or time settings of its own, so this check does not apply

profiles.name: GCP firewall rules
profiles.reason: GCP firewall rules only filter traffic to and from a VPC network's instances: they have no management plane, accounts, logging or time settings of their own, so this check does not apply
